title: add-vpc-control-plane-terraform-multi-az-subnets-endpoints-peering-route53
author: Aisha Khan
description: Adds a Terraform module and installer hooks to provision a VPC control plane for private deployments across multiple AZs. Motivation: private control plane customers need a repeatable, auditable, and configurable Terraform module that provisions subnets (control plane and workload), interface and gateway endpoints, security groups tailored for control-plane components, cross-account VPC peering for customer-managed data plane, and Route53 private hosted zone peering to support internal DNS resolution. This PR implements: 1) terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane: multi-AZ subnet layout with configurable CIDR blocks, az distribution, NAT options, and tags; 2) interface/gateway endpoints for S3, STS, ECR (if used), and custom service endpoints; 3) security groups and least-privilege ingress/egress rules with explicit docs on required ports for control plane, console, and webhooks; 4) cross-account VPC peering resources and automated Route53 private hosted zone association and peering records; 5) Helm chart annotation changes to reference the cloud-provider interface for peering healthchecks; 6) installer upgrade hooks and rollback plan in the installer/upgrade directory; 7) acceptance tests (terratest) and CI pipeline steps. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implementation - [x] Terratest coverage for subnet/peering lifecycle - [x] Helm annotations and values schema updated - [x] Docs and upgrade notes added - [x] CI pipeline updated with tutu/terraform fmt/lint/tests - [x] Security review completed Usage: see terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane/README.md for example inputs and outputs. Important notes: - Default behavior preserves existing VPCs when only peering is enabled; module has allow_management_vpc_creation boolean to support new VPCs. - Route53 peering requires permissions across accounts; documented in README. - Rollback path: controller will fall back to previous peering state, and installer hooks provide a forced-delete step if necessary. Backwards compatibility: this module is opt-in and does not change any existing default installer behavior.
